humanoid.metric: Annual humanoid robot deployments, installations and shipments proxy
humanoid.scope: Counterpoint worldwide humanoid installations in 2025 and shipments in 2026, including research, data collection, entertainment, service, logistics and industrial applications. Shipments are a deployment proxy, not proof of productive operation. The population differs from IFR industrial robot installations; their ratio is not an observed humanoid share of all robots. Any future total-deployment proxy and humanoid relative-count ratio are authored scenario assumptions, not a measured all-robot census.
humanoid.methodology: The reported approximate 2025 installation count is the only full-year historical anchor. Earlier counts are unavailable, not backcast from a benchmark. The 2026 shipment forecast is a conservative scenario anchor, not an observed full-year total. Installations and shipments are proxies with different coverage; normalized line heights do not measure market share.

observations.precision: Approximately 16,000 additional installations
observations.detail: Counterpoint reports approximately 16,000 additional humanoid installations worldwide during 2025. This is an annual flow estimate, not cumulative stock or a task-performance score. No annual counts before 2025 are asserted.

scenario.detail: The approximate 16,000 additional installations reported for 2025 replace the former benchmark-return measure. The 2026 anchor of 50,000 is a conservative reference to a published forecast of more than 50,000 shipments, not an observed full-year count. Future humanoid deployments initially follow modeled robot deployment growth, then grow sublinearly with exponent 0.6 and transition multiplier 10. Counts keep rising while their ratio to the modeled total shrinks. This ratio is an author-set relationship, not observed market share; the historical industrial proxy and humanoid shipment survey cover different populations.

data.metric: Published real-robot training episodes, selected corpora
data.scope: A closed inventory of reported training episodes, not all private robot interaction data, equal-duration physical experience, or a global census.
data.methodology: Fixed inventory of independently collected source families; no OXE/Octo aggregates, RoboNet components, relabeled copies, resolution variants, or simulation added. Source-level overlap audit, not hash-level deduplication. Episode lengths and segmentation differ. Alpha is replaced by Beta, adding only the difference. Initial DROID 1.0.0 is pinned; later repackaging is not new collection. RoboNet uses a later pinned TFDS representation of the 2019 corpus. Exact annual release-inventory totals are retained. Curves between annual snapshots are visual interpolation, not the actual timing of collection or release. Before 2019, the curve is an explicitly hypothetical historical reconstruction, not an inventory of these not-yet-released datasets.
